title: Simulate and Plan GPU Headroom for Mixed Weights/KV/Activation Footprints
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Goal: Produce a validated GPU memory budget model and headroom plan that covers weights, KV cache, and activations for multi-tenant inference pools. We need a simulation-driven approach that maps real request mixes (seq len distribution, model families, quantization levels) to memory pressure and tail-latency risk under continuous batching. Deliverables: a parametric simulator, a recommended headroom policy (static + dynamic knobs), a set of knob defaults for Dedicated / Private offerings, and an experiment plan to validate in staging.
background: We currently tune headroom heuristically per-model based on a few load tests. As we add more model variants (8-bit/4-bit quantized weights, varying KV cache retention for long-context models) and move toward denser packing in Dedicated pools, this heuristic is brittle. Observed problems: unexpected OOMs with large-batch transient traffic spikes, degraded latency when KV spill occurs, and overprovisioning that raises unit costs. A simulation that combines weights memory, KV residency, and activation working set per request will let us set tight but safe headroom and automated eviction/fallback rules.
success_criteria:
1) Simulator can predict OOM/eviction events within +/-15% of observed memory usage on staging runs across 6 model+quant pairs.
2) Headroom policy reduces average reserved headroom by >=20% vs current defaults without increasing OOM rate.
3) Runtime rollout of policy has feature flags and opt-outs; release in runtime-1.20 with observability dashboards showing memory breakdown per-token for representative tenants.
approach_notes:
- Build parametric memory model: weights (per-model, quantization-dependent), KV resident bytes (per active session & per-token), activations (sampled per sequence length and batch composition).
- Ingest request trace samples from production anonymized logs to derive mix distributions.
- Simulate continuous batching logic (batch growth/shrink rates, KV reuse) rather than static batch size.
- Model preemption/eviction policies: earliest-LRU for KV vs graceful routing to warm fallback models.
- Compute headroom percentiles (p50, p95, p99) and cost vs safety trade curve.
- Produce recommended defaults and a small feature: reserve_headroom_hint that ties into autoscaler to auto-burst reserve when needed.
progress_updates: 2025-02-19: Kickoff meeting with serving, infra, and product. Collected initial production traces (sampled) and agreed on anonymization filter.
2025-02-24: Prototype memory model implemented (weights + per-session KV sizing). Early sim shows KV dominates for long-context sessions.
2025-02-27: Running first staging replay with continuous-batching enabled; observed two cache-eviction incidents aligned with sudden seq-len spikes. Logged memory trace to staging dashboard.
2025-03-01: Added quantization factor table for 8/4-bit weights and re-ran 10k-sample sim. Preparing PR for simulator and dataset of anonymized traces.
decisions:
1) Use production-sampled traces instead of synthetic profiles to capture realistic tail behavior.
2) Represent KV cost as (session_active_tokens * per_token_kv_bytes) with a short-term growth window to model streaming requests.
3) Deploy headroom policy as tunable flags: static_percent + dynamic_token_window to start; defer complex ML-based prediction to a follow-up.
open_risks:
- Trace sampling may under-represent rare long-conversation tenants; need stratified sampling.
- Continuous-batching simulator assumptions (growth rate, batch combine threshold) must be validated against newer runtime batching heuristics.
- Multi-tenant interference when many small sessions co-reside could create degenerate KV fragmentation not captured by current model.
next_steps:
1) Land simulator PR and unit tests (ENG-10432-sim-pr).
2) Run stratified sampling and add synthetic worst-case scenarios (very long seqs, high concurrency).
3) Run controlled staging experiment to measure OOM/eviction delta with candidate headroom settings.
4) Draft runtime configuration API for reserve_headroom_hint and autoscaler integration.
